question: When was the 'Mahatma Gandhi Series' of Indian Bank notes started?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1996**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi Series** of Indian banknotes was introduced in **1996**.
 
• This series replaced the Lion Capital Series to include a portrait of Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation.
 
• The introduction of this series aimed to incorporate improved security features to combat counterfeiting.
 
• The banknotes in this series were issued in denominations ranging from **Rs. 5 to Rs. 1000**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi Series** was succeeded by the **Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series** in 2016, which featured redesigned notes with enhanced security features.
 
• These new series notes also included a new denomination of **Rs. 2000 and omitted Rs. 1000 notes**.
 
• The design and introduction of new banknotes are managed by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• Banknotes are printed at the Currency Note Press in **Nashik**, the Bank Note Press in **Dewas**, and other facilities.
